name: Lisbon and the Sintra coast
tagline: Tiled facades, river light, and a coast road waiting just beyond the city.
distinctive: Lisbon is a city of hills, tile and river light. It is close enough to the Atlantic coast and the palaces of Sintra that one long weekend can hold both.

image.alt: Illustration of a hillside city of pale houses above the water in golden evening light

moodNotes.weekend: The airport is close to the centre, so you can be at lunch in Chiado soon after landing.
moodNotes.city: Late dinners, rooftop bars and fado in the old quarters.
moodNotes.art: Belém's Jerónimos Monastery, the Gulbenkian collections and the romantic palaces of Sintra.
moodNotes.sea: Atlantic beaches at Cascais and beyond, a short drive west.
moodNotes.drive: The coast road to Cabo da Roca and the forest roads through the Sintra hills make a perfect day out.

seasonNote: Lisbon is mild most of the year. High summer is warm and busy.

arrival.transfer: The airport sits close to the city. The drive to the centre is typically 20–30 minutes.
arrival.groundNote: In the city, walk, take the trams, or use a driver. Collect a car only for the coast and Sintra.

driving.note: Leave the car out of Lisbon's steep old quarters, but take one for the coast road and the Sintra hills.

carWhy: An open-roofed, compact car suits the narrow Sintra roads and the Atlantic coast road equally well.

transfer.label: Driver in the city
transfer.why: A driver for the airport and for evenings in the old quarters, where streets are steep and narrow.

stay.name: Bairro Alto Hotel
stay.why: A boutique hotel on Praça Luís de Camões, between Chiado and the Bairro Alto, with a rooftop looking toward the river.

watchWhy: A watch whose origin story is traditionally traced to Portuguese merchants, worn in the city those merchants sailed from.
aromaWhy: Bitter orange and cedar for a city of citrus trees and sea air, and fresh enough for the car on the coast road.

days.title: Chiado and the miradouros
days.text: Spend the afternoon between the viewpoints of the old city, then have dinner in Príncipe Real and a late drink on a rooftop.

days.title: Belém
days.text: Visit the Jerónimos Monastery early, then see MAAT on the riverfront. Custard tarts are obligatory.

days.title: Sintra and the coast
days.text: Drive to Sintra for its palaces and gardens, then return by Cabo da Roca and Cascais along the Atlantic.

moreDays.title: The Gulbenkian
moreDays.text: See the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum and its gardens, one of Europe's great private collections.

moreDays.title: Comporta
moreDays.text: Drive south for long Atlantic beaches, rice fields and a very long lunch.
